cells.tense: Right now the sentence is forming and you are the one letting it out.
cells.ask: Name the next step out loud to someone today, one line, no case built around it.
cells.core:
A loose thing comes to you and you give it a shape before you know how it lands. The shape holds, and the fog is not something you wait on. What you put out tends to be usable, and you keep the next step small on purpose. There is enough light for the step in front of you, and that is the whole of what you need; you read what is actually there at the moment you need it.

Keep that in motion. What you shape is real, and it does not wait on your having all of it first.
cells.sheetLine: You can shape a thing before you know how it lands.
cells.verb: putting a shape on something while it is still forming
cells.place: the stretch where the next step is clear and the road ahead is not

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a version of this that has not arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one question you have been trying to settle by force and let it stay open a week.
cells.core:
Something needs a frame now, so you pin it down before you can see what it is, and then every new question gets the same treatment. The declaring is doing more work than the thing it is supposed to hold, and the frame slides off what it meant to catch.

The fog does not get a vote in this. You keep forcing an answer before you have one, and the forcing costs you the small signals that would have shown you the next step. Getting harder to find that way, not easier.

Try it once this week: leave one question unanswered and see whether the room holds anyway.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that is already behind you, and the room is quiet.
cells.ask: Say the next step into a voice memo, sixty seconds, before you are sure of it.
cells.core:
Going well, this looks like enough light for one step and quiet trust for the rest: you name what you see, small and unfinished, and it moves things along — no case built, no full road required.

What is happening instead is that you have gone quiet where you have something to say. It shows as drifting whichever way is clearest for the moment, choosing a story that fits rather than one you would have written yourself. Putting a shape on a loose thing has stopped coming out of you, and the saying stays inside. Telling one person is enough, and it does not have to be right.

cells.tense: The pen you say you never picked up is already moving on the page.
cells.ask: Point at one sentence you have already put into the world this week and claim it.
cells.core:
You are already giving shape to ambiguous things. It shows in the emails you send, the way you rephrase a messy situation into a sentence someone can act on, the small definitions you offer in meetings without calling them that.

This is not modesty. It is you telling yourself the shape came from somewhere else, from the shared mood or the obvious call. But the obvious call did not make itself. The guess you brought back from the dark has been good, and you let it go unnamed.

Look at one thing you said this week that helped someone move, then own it to yourself. No one has to agree.
